title: Evaluate masked token perplexity
statement:
Step 15 · LLM engineering

Perplexity is exp(mean token negative log likelihood). Padding and ignored prompt positions should not influence the mean. Perplexity comparisons also depend on the tokenizer and evaluation data.

Build it

Return exp(mean(losses whose mask is 1)). Equal-length lists contain finite nonnegative natural-log losses; mask contains 0 or 1 and selects at least one loss. Selected mean is below 100.

Contract: Implement perplexity using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: losses = [0.6931471805599453, 99, 0.6931471805599453], mask = [1, 0, 1]
Expected: 2.0
Input: losses = [0, 1], mask = [1, 1]
Expected: 1.6487212707001282
Hint

Average only the included tokens, not the padded sequence length.

Review your understanding

Why can lower perplexity fail to imply better task completion or safer answers?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
